title: Stateful vs stateless revisions
summary: Through 2025-11-25 an MCP connection was a stateful session opened by `initialize`. The 2026-07-28 revision removes the handshake and session id, sends version and capabilities with every request and makes `server/discover` mandatory.
useIf: You build or run servers and clients across both eras, or must choose which revision to target.
avoidIf: You assume a 2026-07-28 client can talk to a 2025-11-25-only server. It cannot without fallback logic.

explain.md: In **2025-11-25** (the last stateful revision) the client opened with `initialize`, carrying its version and capabilities, the server answered and the client sent `notifications/initialized`. On HTTP the server could assign an `Mcp-Session-Id`, a 404 meant the session ended, and a GET stream carried server messages [[r21]] [[r22]]. In **2026-07-28** all of that is removed. Each request carries `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` in `_meta`, and servers MUST implement `server/discover` [[r1]] [[tr5]].

explain.md: **State without sessions.** A creation tool returns an explicit handle and later calls take it as an argument. A handle is a name, not a capability, so check authorization on every call and key state by verified user id. Unauthenticated servers need high-entropy handles with bounded lifetime [[r6]].

**Dual-era.** *Modern* means 2026-07-28 and later, *legacy* means `initialize`-based. A modern client against a legacy server fails, so on stdio a dual-era client probes with `server/discover` and on HTTP it falls back to `initialize` when it gets no recognized modern error. A modern-only server answers legacy GET or DELETE with 405, ignores `Mcp-Session-Id` and `Last-Event-ID`, and SHOULD name its supported versions in the error to `initialize` [[r24]] [[r2]].

explain.title: Removed is not the same as Deprecated
explain.md: The handshake, session id, GET stream, `ping`, `logging/setLevel` and SSE resumption were removed by the 2026-07-28 breaking change. Roots, Sampling, Logging, Dynamic Client Registration, HTTP+SSE and two `includeContext` values are Deprecated: they still work, with the earliest removal on or after 2027-07-28 for the first four and nothing Removed yet under the lifecycle policy [[r9]].

whereToUse: Choosing the target revision for a new server behind an autoscaling load balancer

Reviewing an SDK or gateway for which eras it supports

use: Target modern-only when every consumer SDK supports 2026-07-28
Run dual-era while legacy hosts remain
Use explicit handles instead of session state for multi-step tools
Count requests per protocol version to decide when to drop legacy
avoid: Shipping a modern-only server to legacy hosts without telling them
Relying on sticky sessions or shared session storage in the modern path
Treating a deprecated feature as already removed
flips: Legacy traffic drops to zero for a release cycle: remove the legacy path
You need server-initiated sampling today: keep the legacy path and plan the migration

pitfalls.symptom: Legacy hosts get HTTP 400 after a server upgrade
pitfalls.cause: A modern-only server rejects requests that lack the modern `_meta` and headers
pitfalls.fix: Run dual-era until a per-version request counter shows no legacy traffic

pitfalls.symptom: Intermittent 404s on legacy clients after scaling out
pitfalls.cause: Legacy sessions live on one instance and the load balancer is not sticky
pitfalls.fix: Use sticky routing or shared storage for the legacy path only, and move modern state into handles

pitfalls.symptom: A user reads another user's job result
pitfalls.cause: A handle was treated as authentication
pitfalls.fix: Authorize the caller against the handle's owner on every call

scenarios.title: A greenfield remote server on autoscaled instances
scenarios.situation: A team builds a new remote server on serverless instances behind a plain load balancer. Known consumers use recent SDKs that implement 2026-07-28. Multi-step workflows exist.
unknowns: Do all consumer hosts actually ship 2026-07-28 support?
scenarios.question: Which revision do you target?

options.name: Modern-only 2026-07-28 with explicit handles
options.why: No session storage or sticky routing, any instance can serve any request, and MRTR covers mid-call input.

options.name: Dual-era from day one
options.tradeoff: Two behaviours to build and test for hosts you may not have.

options.name: Legacy-only 2025-11-25 with a shared session store
options.why: It builds on the handshake and sessions the new revision removed and needs sticky routing or shared state.
options.tradeoff: Right only when every consumer is a fixed legacy host.

flips.then: Add the legacy path for it and measure its traffic.
Keep a legacy path, since sampling is Deprecated but still works there.

scenarios.takeaway: Statelessness pays off most where instances are interchangeable.

scenarios.title: An enterprise fleet of mixed hosts
scenarios.situation: A company has dozens of internal servers and hosts. Most hosts run SDKs that implement only `initialize`-based revisions. A few new hosts use 2026-07-28. Upgrades take quarters.
unknowns: What share of requests is legacy today?
scenarios.question: How should a shared server handle both?

options.name: Dual-era server with per-version request counters
options.why: Legacy hosts keep working, modern hosts get the stateless path and the counters show when to retire legacy.
options.tradeoff: Two paths and a split state model until retirement.

options.name: Switch to modern-only now
options.why: Legacy clients fail with no fallback.
options.tradeoff: Right once metrics show no legacy traffic.

options.name: Stay legacy-only until all hosts upgrade
options.why: No change now and every host works.
options.tradeoff: New hosts cannot connect and you carry session infrastructure.

flips.if: Legacy traffic is under a small, tracked share and the owners agree

flips.then: Delete the legacy path and the session store.

scenarios.takeaway: Measure by protocol version before you cut an era.

scenarios.title: A client that launches unknown local servers
scenarios.situation: A host spawns third-party servers over stdio. It does not know whether a given server speaks 2025-11-25 or 2026-07-28.
unknowns: How should the client cache the detected era?
What should users see on failure?
scenarios.question: How does the client connect?

options.name: Dual-era client: send `server/discover` first, fall back to `initialize` on non-modern errors
options.why: The probe fails deterministically and a recognized modern error means stay modern.
options.tradeoff: An extra round trip and fallback code.

options.name: Legacy-only client
options.why: Works with every server that is not modern-only.
options.tradeoff: Cannot reach modern-only servers and carries migration debt.

options.name: Modern-only client
options.why: Against a legacy server the request may be rejected, ignored or even handled under legacy semantics.
options.tradeoff: Right once every server you launch is modern.

flips.if: The server is HTTP rather than stdio
flips.then: Try a modern request and inspect a 400 body before falling back.

flips.if: Every server you launch is bundled with the host and known to be modern

scenarios.takeaway: A client that meets unknown servers should support both eras.

quiz.q: Match each 2025-11-25 mechanism to its 2026-07-28 replacement.
quiz.explain: Each mechanism was removed and replaced as listed in the 2026-07-28 changelog. Handles are an authoring pattern, not a protocol feature.

quiz.q: A modern-only server receives traffic from an older client. Which behaviours match the spec?
options: Mint and echo a session id for compatibility
Name its supported versions in the error to `initialize`
quiz.explain: A modern-only server answers GET and DELETE with 405, ignores the session id and `Last-Event-ID`, and SHOULD name supported versions in its `initialize` error. It does not mint or echo session ids.

flashcards.back: Per-request `_meta` with `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `clientCapabilities`, plus a mandatory `server/discover` on the server.

flashcards.front: What happens when a modern client meets a legacy-only server?
flashcards.back: It fails. A dual-era client probes with `server/discover` on stdio, or falls back to `initialize` on HTTP when it gets no recognized modern error.
Removed by the revision: handshake, session id, GET stream. Deprecated but working: Roots, Sampling, Logging, DCR, HTTP+SSE. Nothing is Removed under the lifecycle policy yet.
